sources.title: Machine learning and the cross-section of cryptocurrency returns
sources.authors: Nusret Cakici; Syed Jawad Hussain Shahzad; Barbara Bedowska-Sojka; Adam Zaremba
sources.relevance: Identifies past alpha and momentum among the important simple predictors of cross-sectional crypto returns.

sources.title: Crypto Residual Momentum Strategy
sources.author: FionaNi-DS
sources.relevance: Documents 30-day rolling market-beta residualisation, residual momentum, a 14-day formation period, 7-day holding period, and strict 2024-2025 OOS evaluation.

hypothesis: Cross-sectional momentum remains predictive after removing contemporaneously estimated common crypto-market beta; coins with stronger recent residual momentum outperform weaker residual-momentum peers over the following week.
mechanism: Common crypto beta masks asset-specific persistence. Slow information diffusion and limits to arbitrage can allow idiosyncratic return continuation after market exposure is removed.
market_factor: Equal-weight hourly log return across contemporaneously available panel assets.
signal: Sum of causal residual hourly log returns over the formation window. Each residual uses a rolling 30-day beta estimated only from returns available before that residual hour.
universe: Point-in-time assets with exact hourly history sufficient for beta plus formation window and top 80 percent by lagged trailing 30-day close*volume; minimum 8 assets.
rebalance: Weekly Monday 00:00 UTC. Signal uses data only through the prior completed hour; execution occurs at current open.
construction: Equal-weight long top residual-momentum quartile / short bottom residual-momentum quartile, 0.5 gross per side.
development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC >= 0.02, HAC p < 0.05, positive top-minus-bottom subsequent-week return, at least 100 weekly observations.
limitations: Market factor is equal-weight because historical point-in-time market capitalization is not available. Funding is not included in the OHLCV panel and will be disclosed if OOS is consumed.
